# Domain mappings

These mappings route HTTP/HTTPS traffic to local ports. They are managed by
Supbuddy via Caddy and per-suffix DNS resolver files in `/etc/resolver/` —
**do not edit either manually**. Supbuddy does NOT write `/etc/hosts`; adding
entries there by hand shadows the resolver and will not be cleaned up with the
project.

| Domain | Port | URL | Enabled |
|--------|------|-----|---------|
| map-chat.map-chat.test | 3000 | https://map-chat.map-chat.test | yes |
| api.map-chat.test | 55021 | https://api.map-chat.test | yes |
| studio.map-chat.test | 55023 | https://studio.map-chat.test | yes |
| mail.map-chat.test | 55024 | https://mail.map-chat.test | yes |
| logs.map-chat.test | 55027 | https://logs.map-chat.test | yes |

## To add or change

Use the MCP tool `create_mapping(domain, port)`, or open Supbuddy and edit
in the Configure tab.

**Picking the port:** on a `thin` project, mappings route to the project's own
loopback IP — target the app's **canonical** dev port (Next.js `:3000`, Vite
`:5173`) and start it with `supbuddy run -- <dev command>`. Never scan for a
"free" port to avoid another project's dev server; only `host`-mode projects
share `127.0.0.1` and need unique ports.
